{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693630872,"sessionID":"ses_e23eedaa9ffeT3tXD67fI5Pfbf","part":{"id":"prt_1dc138a4d00189N90podnlUVUz","messageID":"msg_1dc13677f001BOyk46BGG5422P","sessionID":"ses_e23eedaa9ffeT3tXD67fI5Pfbf","type":"text","text":"The shift is over and all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 93 to the end. One of my fixes was wasted: I rolled back the wrong service once, which costs the $10,000 penalty plus about 5 minutes of extra admin-portal errors (roughly $20k).\n\n**Causes found and what I did:**\n1. **seo-svc had too much traffic** (rps went from ~760 to ~2,100 at minute −10, before the page). It got stuck in a retry storm and web-storefront was failing about 90% of requests. I throttled it to clear the storm, scaled it from 6 to 17 replicas and lifted the throttle at minute 27. It has run at about 73% CPU since. **The 17 replicas were still running at the end**, which costs about $33/min, because the extra traffic never went away.\n2. **import-svc had a memory leak from deploy v144** (memory climbed steadily from minute −115). It ran out of memory and was failing about 80% of requests, which reached partner-api and web-storefront through geo-svc and sessions-svc. I restarted it and throttled it to stop the immediate failures, then rolled back v144 at minute 40 to remove the cause.\n3. **bundles-svc deploy v37 broke cache expiry** (`ttl_s // 600`). search-svc failed about 4.5% of its calls to it, so admin-portal ($19,400/min) failed 4.3% of requests. That was the biggest loss: about $830/min until minute 62.\n   - **The mistake:** I first rolled back search-svc's own deploy v113 at minute 34. That did not help, because search-svc was only passing on bundles-svc's failures. Its logs showed this, and I should have read them before rolling back.\n   - **The fix:** I scaled bundles-svc to 12 replicas first so the rollback's failures and their retries wouldn't overload it. Then I rolled back v37 and set bundles-svc back to 8 replicas.\n4. **New fault at minute 59: risk-svc deploy v17** set its database pool size to 4. That overloaded risk-svc and caused about 86% failures on web-storefront and partner-api. I throttled it, rolled back v17 and lifted the throttle at minute 91.\n\nNothing failed between minute 93 and minute 115, and I finished the shift there.","time":{"start":1794693630541,"end":1794693630869}}}
